AAPL.rationale: Apple's fundamental health and trajectory are strong: Q2 FY2026 revenue grew +16.6% YoY to $111.18B, EPS grew +21.8% YoY to $2.01, gross margin expanded 230bps to 49.3%, and operating cash flow grew +19.8% YoY. The balance sheet is fortress-grade with equity up to $106.49B and debt declining to $82.70B. Services at ~$31B/quarter at 76%+ gross margins and market share gains across all product categories reinforce franchise durability. However, Pillar 2 (valuation) is a significant constraint: P/E of 37.1x yields only 2.7%, a 179bps negative spread to the 10-year Treasury at 4.49%. The stock has already rallied +20.7% in one quarter, sitting just 2.8% below its 52-week high, suggesting the Q2 beat is largely priced in. Pillar 3 offers modest positive optionality: the Q3 earnings date (July 30) will test whether price increases offset memory cost inflation, and the foldable iPhone pipeline (10M units at ~$2,500) and Intel foundry partnership are credible medium-term catalysts. But near-term, memory cost inflation, regulatory overhang (DOJ, EU DMA, Italy probe), and the AI strategy lag temper enthusiasm. Net: a quality compounder at a full valuation with balanced risk-reward — mildly attractive but not compelling at current levels.
key_factors: Q2 FY2026 revenue $111.18B (+16.6% YoY), EPS $2.01 (+21.8% YoY) — strong fundamental trajectory
Gross margin expanded to 49.3% from 47.0% YoY; operating margin 32.3% vs 31.0% — genuine margin improvement
Operating cash flow $28.70B (+19.8% YoY), tracking net income growth — high earnings quality
Balance sheet deleveraging: equity $106.49B (+59.5% vs prior year), debt $82.70B (-12.8%), D/E 0.777
Services revenue ~$31B in March 2026 quarter at ~76% gross margin — recurring high-margin revenue engine
Market share gains projected: iPhone 25%, iPad 39%, Mac 23% in 2026 per Counterpoint Research
P/E of 37.1x with earnings yield 2.7% — 179bps below 10-year Treasury yield of 4.49%; valuation demands sustained high-teens growth
Stock rallied +20.7% in one quarter to $308.63, just 2.8% below 52-week high of $317.40 — Q2 beat largely priced in
Memory cost inflation and tariff headwinds ($1.1B tariff costs); June price increases testing pricing power
Regulatory overhang: DOJ lawsuit, EU DMA, Italy iCloud probe threatening App Store commission model
Q3 earnings July 30, 2026 — first read on price increase pass-through and margin impact; near-term catalyst
Foldable iPhone pipeline (10M units at ~$2,500) and Intel foundry partnership — credible medium-term growth levers

iPhone gaining two percentage points to reach 25% and iPad's market share growing from 35% in 2025 to 39% in 2026
